chapter: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
title: Why he stayed with the Spirits and then left after the Buffalo fight
summary: Bookings and a pact to stick together kept him until the fighting and the Buffalo clash with Doug made him quit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: How come you stayed with the Spirits, I mean as long as you did, like through the '30s, really, all through the '30s, before you came out here?
Because we had them bookings.
Yeah. It was like an act that was successful.
Yeah. It was a group.
So then all the record dates you'd do on the side.
Yeah. On the side I had them gigs.
You must have had offers to go with other groups.
I did. I had offers, but I mean since we had planned to each other that we'd stick together.
Uh-huh.
Understand? Until we got in that big money.
Right.
But we didn't stick together long enough.
Right.
On account of we'd be arguing, fighting. And when that started, I got disgusted. And when me and Doug had it, and he was the leader guitar -- tipple player, him and I got in a fight in --
Buffalo.
Buffalo.
Yeah.
And that's when it happened, the disagreement.
Uh-huh.
And I got back to New York, and I said, 'If I ever get back to New York there won't be no more.' And I left them.
